Investigate if other animals have ingested pieces of this book and slay any demons who escape their bonds.

n: Save the Lettuce, Save the World
d: A flock of game dodos has begun devouring the crops of La Noscean lettuce farmers living near Camp Bloodshore. Attempts by the local militia to drive off the ravenous cloudkin have resulted in numerous injuries and the untimely death of a one-eyed tracking hound. Travel to the area and eliminate the dodos before they can cause further damage.

In an attempt to increase the amount of land under thalassocratic rule, the Admiral of Limsa Lominsa has ordered the annexation and colonization of large stretches of unclaimed coastal land near Camp Bloodshore. However, due to the large swarms of vilekin still residing in the area, very few volunteers have chosen to settle the hills, making it difficult for the city-state to maintain its claim there. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel east and assist in clearing the outlying areas of any and all possible threats.

Last night, a band of footpads intercepted a delivery of privately smelted silver ingots being transported from Wineport to a trading vessel docked in Limsa Lominsa. Warehouse foreman Wynstin Walder of the Brugaire Consortium will handsomely reward those who can aid in “discreetly” retrieving the shipment. He has left the method of retrieval up to the contractor.

n: A Roseling by Any Other Name
d: Known for its aphrodisiacal properties, sap from the vines of the rarely seen ocean roseling has become increasingly popular on the pleasure boats anchored in the bay off the Captains Ward. The Brugaire Consortium will handsomely reward anyone willing to travel to Bloodshore and procure several specimens.

A pack of feral galagos, indigenous to the slopes of O'Ghomoro, has strayed from its mountainous habitat and wandered far south to Bloodshore. To sate their simian appetites, the ravenous beasts have begun raiding the fields of nearby farmsteads. If they are not dealt with immediately, entire crops could be lost.

An imp was discovered eavesdropping on an important meeting held by high-ranking officials of the thalassocracy, but escaped before the Yellowjackets were able to subdue the villainous voidsent. Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn has ordered the imp, known to ofttimes don the glamour of a ram, “permanently silenced” before it can return to its owner and reveal the secrets it learned.

A Bloodshore shepherd claims an unidentified beast (or beasts) has been slaughtering the game dodos to which she tends. However, despite watching over the birds, without rest, for over 36 bells, the young Miqo'te insists she has witnessed nothing enter or exit the herd. From the description of events given, it is highly likely the culprit is none other than a rogue imp―known to use magicks to disguise itself as another animal and thereby infiltrate its pack, where it can feed on the blood of its unsuspecting victims without fear of reprisal. The shepherd will reward anyone who can aid her in finding and eliminating the insidious pest.

A murderous imp, known to possess fell magicks that it wields to take on the shape of other creatures, has escaped from a high-security wing of the Coral Tower's brigs. To assist in the recapturing of the changeling, the Knights of the Barracuda are hiring sellswords to scour the area of Bloodshore and locate the voidsent using evenfall fireflies to dissolve the imp's glamour. All those with the courage to accept the challenge are to report to Camp Bloodshore at once, and after collecting the fireflies needed to uncover the imp, are to seek out any suspicious-looking animals and use the insects on them. Once the monster has shown its true colors, it is to be taken with force.

In an attempt to strengthen the thalassocracy's hold on La Noscea, the Admiral of Limsa Lominsa has ordered the annexation and colonization of large stretches of unclaimed land in an area known as Skull Valley. Due, however, to the large population of wild creatures still residing in the area, very few volunteers have chosen to settle the hills, making it difficult for the city-state to maintain its claim there. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to Camp Skull Valley and assist in clearing the outlying areas of any and all possible threats.

The Admiral of Limsa Lominsa has expanded her land annexation program to include all unclaimed territory near Skull Valley in central La Noscea. Despite previous efforts to eliminate them, however, wild creatures still residing in the area have dissuaded would-be pioneers from settling the rocky hills and building new homes. To improve conditions, the Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to Camp Skull Valley and assist in clearing the outlying areas of any remaining threats.

Several crates containing rare scalepuk talons and bat skins―bound for the Goldsmiths' Guild in Ul'dah and the Leatherworkers' Guild in Gridania, respectively―were accidentally dropped into the bay when loading a Brugaire Consortium cargo ship. The resulting water damage to the items has made them unfit for sale, forcing the exporters to advertise for adventurers who will travel to Skull Valley and procure a new batch of the aforementioned items.

Over the course of the past fortnight, three different families living in Skull Valley have reported their houses set alight by what they describe as a “small, winged beastie.” Though no serious damage was done to any of the properties, while the families were occupied with extinguishing the blazes, someone or something entered the homes and robbed them of various items ranging from jewelry to blood sausage. The pattern of simultaneous arson and theft, combined with the descriptions given by the victims, has led local authorities to believe that the culprit may be a notorious imp. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to the area and rid it of the threat. They ask any who would attempt this task, however, to proceed with the utmost caution, for imps are known to travel with deadly creatures known as nightwolves.

An uncharacteristically wet winter has led to an explosion in the number of syrphids infesting the region. If the pests are not dealt with, it is feared their bites will bring disease, which could in turn deal a severe blow to the region's economy. Find and eliminate the vilekin immediately.

The wheat garners in Skull Valley are overrun with pack rats and if action is not taken quickly, Limsa Lominsa may be faced with a flour shortage this coming winter. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to the area and rid it of the pests.

A small flock of stray dodos has been spotted devouring rare herbs growing in the fields surrounding Skull Valley. The Knights of the Barracuda have been petitioned by local botanists to cull the beasts and protect the herbs used in various medical unguents. The Knights, in turn, are seeking adventurers willing to join them in the hunt.

Many of the fisheries located in the quarter of Limsa Lominsa known as the Barrel have been troubled by frequent aurelia attacks which leave holes in the nets, allowing their farmed fish to escape. The owner of one of the affected fisheries―a Lalafell by the name of Pelmomo―has set aside a stipend to reward adventurers willing to assist him by traveling to the aurelia breeding grounds in Skull Valley and eliminating as many of the floating monstrosities as possible.

In an attempt to strengthen the thalassocracy's hold on La Noscea, the Admiral of Limsa Lominsa has ordered the annexation and colonization of large stretches of unclaimed land in an area known as Bald Knoll. Due, however, to the large population of wild creatures still residing in the area, very few volunteers have chosen to settle the hills, making it difficult for the city-state to maintain its claim there. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to Camp Bald Knoll and assist in clearing the outlying areas of any and all possible threats.

Botanists accustomed to gathering their herbs on the lush plains of Bald Knoll have been unable to meet their quotas due to attacks by deadly seedkin called flytraps, known to blend into the surrounding foliage and take their victims unawares. To ensure the livelihood of the gatherers, travel to the area and rid them of their problem.

Lightweight, durable, and waterproof, mottled eft skins are in constant demand among tailors in Limsa Lominsa who use the material to outfit the city-state's sailors. The Brugaire Consortium will pay a fair price for any high-quality skins procured from Bald Knoll and delivered to one of their representatives for resale.

No one knows exactly when wizened farmer Old Man Wyrston of Bald Knoll passed away, but by the time his kin finally arrived at his remote homestead to collect his belongings, they found that all of his livestock─several dodos and rams─as well as his two hounds had escaped their pens. Now there are numerous reports from other croptenders in the area of a large pack of once-domesticated animals ravaging their fields. To prevent any more losses, locate the pack and send them to their master in the afterlife.

A murderous devilet known to possess fell magicks that it wields to take on the shape of other creatures has escaped from a high-security wing of the Coral Tower's brigs. To assist in the recapturing of the changeling, the Knights of the Barracuda are hiring sellswords to scour the area of Bald Knoll and locate the voidsent using blue landtrap vines (the smell of which the creature abhors) to dissolve the devilet's glamour. All those with the courage to accept the challenge are to report to Camp Bloodshore at once, and after collecting the vines needed to uncover the escapee, seek out any suspicious-looking animals and use the vegetation on them. Once the devilet has shown its true colors, it is to be taken with force.

Frequent attacks on chocobo carriages passing through the remote area of Iron Lake have Lominsan merchants up in arms, claiming the Yellowjackets stationed in the area are not fulfilling their duties. Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn vehemently denies this claim, and in a wholehearted effort to assure the people of Limsa Lominsa and Vylbrand that the thalassocracy will do all that is necessary to maintain peace in the region, he is actively hiring adventurers and sellswords to assist in an organized culling of the beasts in the area.

A lack of funding has left Camp Bald Knoll understaffed, and the few Yellowjackets stationed there overworked. To make matters worse, the combination of low morale and high levels of fatigue has led to an increase in the number of fatal accidents occurring while the Bald Knoll marines are on their patrols. In an attempt to prevent these accidents and provide his men and women with a well-deserved rest, Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn is seeking civilian adventurers to temporarily assist with patrol duties at the remote outpost in western La Noscea. All those who accept the task should come to Bald Knoll prepared for battle.

Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn vehemently denies this claim, and in a wholehearted effort to assure the people of Limsa Lominsa and Vylbrand that the thalassocracy will do all that is necessary to maintain peace in the region, he is actively hiring adventurers and sellswords to assist in an organized culling of the beasts in the area.

Several days ago, Ser Jeorge of House Martynn and his squire Tywick were riding near Bald Knoll in western La Noscea when they were attacked by a pair of giant mottled efts. The noble knight hailing from Ishgard was able to dispatch both of the creatures with his mighty battleaxe, but not before losing half of his right ear, two fingers on his left hand, and suffering grievous wounds to both of his legs. By the time a third eft came lumbering out from behind a crop of nearby rocks, Ser Jeorge lacked the strength to do anything but watch in terror as the scalekin locked young Tywick's leg in its jaws and dragged the poor lad back off to its lair. A party of Yellowjacket scouts discovered Ser Jeorge just after evenfall, and applied poultices to his wounds before escorting him back to Limsa Lominsa where he could be treated by the local leeches. And while a search was conducted for Tywick, two days of scouring the area turned up naught but a single bloody boot... The knight, both enraged and distraught at the loss of his loyal squire, has since pledged to rid the region of efts, and is offering a reward for each head placed before him.

A lack of natural predators has led to an explosion in the population of land-dwelling jellyfish, and now hundreds of the floating creatures are roaming about unchecked in the hills surrounding Iron Lake. While not inherently violent, if provoked, the wavekin will use their tentacles to fire tiny, toxic, arrow-like projectiles, dangerous enough to paralyze or even kill. To prevent any accidents, the Yellowjackets are seeking able-bodied adventurers to travel to Camp Iron Lake and assist in the culling of aurelias and anemones before their numbers grow any larger.

In an attempt to strengthen the thalassocracy's hold on La Noscea, the Admiral of Limsa Lominsa has ordered the annexation and colonization of large stretches of unclaimed land in an area known as Iron Lake. Due, however, to the large population of wild creatures still residing in the area, very few volunteers have chosen to settle the hills, making it difficult for the city-state to maintain its claim there. The Knights of the Barracuda are petitioning adventurers to travel to Camp Iron Lake and assist in clearing the outlying areas of any and all possible threats.

The Brugaire Consortium had fourteen crates of fresh mongrel meat ready to ship to the coeurl tamers on the Pearl when a band of outlaw Qiqirn broke into the Consortium warehouses and consumed all the meat directly from the boxes, not even bothering to take it back to their lair. So as to not upset their customers, the traders are now rushing to find adventurers willing to travel to Iron Lake and help them regather the meat necessary to fill the order. Payment for services rendered will be received upon delivery of goods.

The increasing number of dog attacks on their flocks have shepherds in Iron Lake worried they soon may not have enough animals left to send to market. To ensure that tender, juicy mutton remains on the plates of all Lominsans, travel to the area's camp and seek out the canine culprits.

A devilet was discovered slipping a deadly poison into a meal being prepared by the Admiral's private chef, but escaped before the Barracuda Knights on guard were able to subdue the villainous voidsent. Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn has ordered the devilet, known to ofttimes don the glamour of a hedgemole, “permanently silenced” so it does not have the opportunity to attempt any more assassinations.

While picking wildflowers near Iron Lake, a young maiden of three and ten came across several pieces of parchment filled with arcane symbols and strange diagrams. The pages frightened the girl so much so that she ran straight home where she told her father of her find. The girl's father, sensing something ill, walked to the area's Yellowjacket camp and repeated the story to the gatewarden stationed there. When the gatewarden relayed this story to Mealvaan's Gate, it was finally discerned that the sheets the girl saw were most likely torn from a stolen copy of the Necrologos―a forbidden tome known to contain wards which bind arcane demons within its pages. The assessors cannot allow the power of the tome to fall into the wrong hands, and are asking adventurers to return to the approximate location of where the maiden first found the parchment, find any remaining pages, put to rest any beasts summoned therefrom, and then destroy the parchment.

A lack of funding has left Camp Iron Lake understaffed, and the few Yellowjackets stationed there overworked. To make matters worse, the combination of low morale and high levels of fatigue has led to an increase in the number of fatal accidents occurring while the Iron Lake marines are on their patrols. In an attempt to prevent these accidents and provide his men and women with a well-deserved rest, Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn is seeking civilian adventurers to temporarily assist with patrol duties at the remote camp in upper La Noscea. All those who accept the task should come to Iron Lake prepared for battle.

Recently, giant packs of deadly cliff yarzons have been making what seem to be “organized” assaults on Camp Iron Lake. The attacks have become so frequent that the Yellowjackets barely have enough time to wipe the gore off their blades before another pack arrives. The soldiers are desperately in need of rest, but abandoning the outpost is not an option, so Yellowjacket Sergeant Sylskaetsyn is seeking adventurers to travel to the remote camp in Upper La Noscea to assist in defending Iron Lake against the relentless vilekin horde.

When Iron Lake farmstead owner Gyles Miller's dog went missing, he assumed that the old hound had crawled off into the woods to die somewhere as animals are oft wont to do. When the farmer's dray horse went missing, he assumed the same thing. However, when the farmer's five-year-old son went missing, he knew something was amiss. Further inspection of his land turned up strange animal prints that suggested a large beast with four webbed feet─a gigantoad─was the culprit. Since then, the Yellowjackets have been conducting searches for the deadly scalekin, using yarzon offal to lure them out of their lairs, and slaying each one they find. The lack of men and women stationed in the remote region, however, has made progress slow. To ensure that no more lives are needlessly lost, the Knights of the Barracuda are seeking able-bodied Disciples of War and Magic to travel to Iron Lake and assist in the search.

Many pilgrims visiting Cassiopeia Hollow to walk the Navigator's Footsteps have found themselves harried by swarms of giant vile gnats who have taken up nest in the cool, damp caves. The Knights of the Barracuda cannot spare sending any more Yellowjacket units into the area, and are hiring eager adventurers to journey to the Hollow and exterminate the vilekin in question.

Once only used to flavor the slop served in the poorest of Lominsan wards, yarzon offal has recently gained popularity amongst the city-state's beau monde (for reasons unfathomable to the common classes). This, in turn, has left the city facing a shortage of the popular ingredient, with prices reaching ridiculous levels, even for some of her better-endowed citizens. The Brugaire Consortium has always been well-versed in the laws of supply and demand, and is actively hiring adventurers to travel to Cassiopeia Hollow to ensure the current demand for yarzon offal can be met.

A trading vessel bound for Aldenard has arrived in Limsa Lominsa ahead of schedule, forcing the Brugaire Consortium to rush to gather the cargo requested by her owners, the Arrzaneth Ossuary. The only items remaining to be procured are several earth orbs taken from elemental spirits dwelling in Cassiopeia Hollow.

Drawn by the loamy aroma of fresh fungi, a pack of wild aldgoats has stumbled upon mushroom beds dug by La Noscean farmers in the moist, dark chambers of Cassiopeia Hollow. Over half of this moon's crop has been devoured, but there still may be time to stop the invaders before all is lost.

Many of the fisheries located in the quarter of Limsa Lominsa known as the Barrel have been troubled by frequent megalocrab attacks which slice holes in the nets, allowing their farmed fish to escape. The owner of one of the affected fisheries―a Lalafell by the name of Pelmomo―has set aside a stipend to reward adventurers willing to assist him by traveling to the crab breeding grounds in Cassiopeia Hollow and eliminating as many of the snipping monstrosities as possible.

A mischievous darkwing devilet, known to possess fell magicks that it wields to take on the shape of other creatures, has escaped from a high-security wing of the Coral Tower's brigs. To assist in the recapturing of the changeling, the Knights of the Barracuda are hiring sellswords to scour the area of Bloodshore and locate the voidsent using bomb eyes to see through the imp's glamour. All those with the courage to accept the challenge are to report to Cassiopeia Hollow at once, and after collecting the eyes needed to uncover the imp, are to seek out any suspicious-looking animals and use the insects on them. Once the imp has shown its true colors, it is to be taken with force.

While walking a leg of Llymlaen's Footsteps in Cassiopeia Hollow, a pilgrim of the Twelve found a piece of parchment containing writings in an ancient hand he could not decipher. Upon return to Limsa Lominsa, the man handed the page over to Mealvaan's Gate, and after further inspection by several log assessors, it was discerned that the writing was Sharlayan and the sheet was actually a page torn from a stolen copy of the Necrologos―a forbidden tome known to contain wards which bind arcane demons within its pages. The assessors believe there may still be more unclaimed pages and are asking adventurers to find them, put to rest any beasts summoned therefrom, and then destroy the parchment.

Investigate if other animals have ingested pieces of this book and slay any demons who escape their bonds.

As of late, Quicksand proprietress Momodi has been troubled by Black Brush naked moles who dig up through the floor of her establishment nightly in search of food. She will handsomely reward any who will hunt down the burrowing beastkin and bring her their heads.

After receiving numerous complaints of foul-tasting water from Black Brush wells, the Brass Blades sent a party to investigate, only to find the wells filled with the moldering faeces of marmots who had burrowed into the wells to drink. To prevent a full-blown outbreak of the crimson flux, locate the whiskered culprits and cull the tiny beasts.

An extended rainy season has led to an explosion in the number of weevils and chiglets in the plains around Camp Black Brush. If the pests are not taken care of immediately, they will burrow into the few remaining trees in the area, killing off the silent giants. Hurry to the camp and locate the vilekin before the damage they cause is irreversible.

Upon final inspection of his cargo, the merchant Flambert realized that he had failed to procure one of the items on his list of orders─wraith cloth. He cannot deny his customers their wishes, so he is willing to generously reward anyone who will bring him pieces of wraith cloth, said to be found on the dune bogies who roam the plains of Black Brush.

A shipment of rare cogwheel ore scheduled to leave Ul'dah on the morrow was found stolen from one of Raptor Couriers' warehouses. The shipping company does not have the means to procure the ore itself, and so is hiring able-bodied fighters to travel to Black Brush and seek out coblyns carrying the ore on their backs.

Swarms of bloodthirsty midges have been sighted in and around Camp Black Brush. It is feared that their bites may carry disease, and therefore the Brass Blades are actively searching for swords to assist them in exterminating the vilekin before pestilence engulfs Ul'dah.

Over the past fortnight, several of the wells dug in Black Brush have mysteriously dried up. Upon further investigation, it was determined that the incessant digging of naked moles has occluded aquifers, diverting precious water supplies to other locations or blocking them off altogether. In order to ensure the people of the region do not perish of thirst, the Brass Blades are hiring adventurers to cull the burrowing beastkin.

Many travelers passing through Black Brush have arrived in Ul'dah only to find certain items of value missing from their possessions. It is believed that this may be the work of thieving spriggans, known for their lust of sparkling baubles, glittering gewgaws, and twinkling trinkets. To prevent any more banditry, the Brass Blades are petitioning adventurers to travel to the area around Camp Black Brush and assist in the culling of these sneaky soulkin.

The wealth of the sultanate relies on the flow of goods into and out of its markets. To ensure that flow does not come to a trickle, the Syndicate has made it their top priority to provide the hundreds of merchants who frequent the city-state with safe passage on their travels. To achieve this goal, they have ordered the Brass Blades to hire adventurers to clear heavy-traffic areas, such as Black Brush, of any beasts that might pose a threat to travelers.

A recent increase of sand yarzon attacks on merchant caravans along the Drybone leg of the Royal Sunway has prompted the sultana's Brass Blades to put out a petition to all those who would assist in culling the troublesome vilekin.

Recently, large swarms of biting midges and syrphids have been sighted near Camp Drybone. Ul'dah's alchemists believe that the infestation is a direct result of the over-culling of the vilekins' natural predators by the influx of new adventurers. The Brass Blades, however, care little of causes, and seek out those willing to lend their blades in finding a solution to the problem at hand. Journey to the camp, seek out the pest clouds, and exterminate them.

Used to scour the dead skin off their bodies while bathing, floatstones are prized by the Limsa Lominsan upper class. To meet the demand, the Jolly Raptor is hiring able-bodied adventurers to travel to Drybone and procure the stones from spriggans or from the backs of certain coblyns inhabiting the arid area.

Last night, while returning from the viewing of a gladiatorial match, a group of peasants was attacked by a pack of deadly sand yarzons. The lone survivor claims the vilekin harried her all the way to Drybone before giving up the chase. Journey to the area's camp and locate the yarzons before they frighten any more of the Coliseum's valued patrons.

Those few smallfolk who, despite the relentless heat and arid soil, continue to live in the area of Drybone have petitioned anyone who will listen to assist them in overcoming a different type of threat to their livelihood. For the past few moons, thieving soulkin known as spriggans have been breaking into their homes and stealing away with what little baubles they can find, though more often than not, those baubles are the only worldly treasures the victims possess. Travel to Camp Drybone and hunt down the pests so the settlers can sleep easier.
A marmot and mole infestation in Drybone has popoto farmers fearing that they will lose the season's crop if the pesky beasts are not dealt with soon. Journey to the area's camp and quell the threat.

Driven from the mines where they would consume the sultanate's supply of precious ore, a pack of coblyns has begun wreaking havoc in the rocky plains near Camp Drybone. Sellswords hired by Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern have made numerous efforts to quell the threat, but due to the sheer number of the insect-like creatures, their success has been limited. Travel to the area and assist the Blades in their mission.

A pack of violent dodos has been ravaging the land, instilling fear into the hearts of local farmers and miners. Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern has deployed several parties of sellswords to cull the foul cloudkin, but has had little success other than driving the flock into the arid region known as Drybone. Travel to the area and rid it of the dodos before they move again.

The Syndicate has made continued efforts to maintain Camp Horizon as a waypoint for merchants and traders traveling between Ul'dah and the ferry docks at Vesper Bay. The ever-present threat of footpads lurking in the nearby hills, however, has travelers wary of using the facilities. To ensure the safety of visitors to the location, the Syndicate seeks skilled Disciples of War and Magic to journey to the hills and eliminate any obvious threats.

Reports of dead livestock in Horizon's Edge have increased tenfold, and farmstead owners have begun to worry that their flocks may not survive the year. From the thousands of needles found buried in the corpses of the animals, it is believed the culprit is none other than the walking seedkin known as the cactuar. Hurry to Camp Horizon and help rid the area of the pests.

Healers in Gridania highly value the curative properties of cactuar legs, which they add to unguents and salves used to treat bites and burns. Cactuars, however, are rare in the Black Shroud, and thus most of those used in the forest city-state must be imported from Ul'dah. A caravan bound north is scheduled to depart from the sultanate in a matter of days, and the Jolly Raptor is hiring able-bodied men and women to gather cactuar legs before the caravan sets off.

With eager challengers from all over the realm flocking to Ul'dah's Coliseum to test their prowess in hand-to-hand combat, Rudius proprietor Zagylswerd the Tall is scrambling to find reasonably priced weapons he can sell to these potential customers. One idea he had is to collect the rusted swords carried by the wights that wander the deserts, then polish and mend them. As he cannot very well do this himself, he is instead willing to pay adventurers a premium for every sword they bring him.

The mangled, half-eaten corpses of three respected merchants were found in a gully not far from Camp Horizon. At first, it was thought the party was attacked by hyenas, but upon further inspection of the bodies, several stab wounds were found in the backs of each, pointing to the work of assassins. The families of the deceased have put a bounty on the heads of the killers, and now seek adventurers to carry out their vengeance.

A dodo shepherd living in Horizon's Edge has discovered that every night one of his flock mysteriously disappears without a trace...and this after locking them up in their pens for the evening. A similar case of missing livestock last summer was reported as being the foul doings of imps who used their glamour magicks to blend in with the flock, and then devour the unsuspecting dodos. There is a good chance that these might be the same imps, and the shepherd is offering a reward to anyone who can flush the skin-changers out of his flock and slay the vile voidsent.

Increased reports of domestic dodos turned savage have alarmed Horizon's Edge shepherds to the point that they were compelled to send for a botanist from faraway Gridania to see if she could not discern what was amiss. After a fortnight of observation and research, the botanist found the “dodo rage” to actually be a type of plague carried by ladybugs and transmitted to the cloudkin via bites. To prevent the plague from spreading to all their livestock, the herdsmen seek adventurers willing to journey to Horizon's Edge and help exterminate the tiny pests.

A pair of mischievous shape-shifting imps charged with setting over a hundred different fires, many of which led to the deaths of humble farmfolk, have escaped from their unescapable cell in the Marasaja Pit. After conducting a realm-wide search to capture the villainous voidsent, the Brass Blades believe they finally have cornered them somewhere in Horizon's Edge. To ensure that they do not let the criminals slip through their fingers, the Blades are seeking adventurers to assist in the search process, which involves collecting brightash from wisps and casting it on local bandits─any of which could be the imps─to dissolve the creatures' glamours.

The Syndicate has made continued efforts to maintain Nophica's Wells to ensure the safety of miners, botanists, and other Disciples of the Land who must frequent the area to collect those items valued by the sultanate's many craftsmen. The ever-present threat of deadly vilekin lurking in the nearby cliffs, however, often dissuades many from making the perilous journey. To further secure the location, the Syndicate seeks skilled Disciples of War and Magic to travel to the remote region and eliminate any obvious threats.

Faeces left by dodos who use the pools as drinking water have begun to poison Nophica's Wells. As this is also the only source of water for those yeomen living in the area, something must be done before the poor men and women are forced to abandon their farmsteads. Volunteers are sought to hunt down the dodos and drive off the cloudkin using any means necessary.

A shipment of voidsent blood─known for its extreme instability─was lost when the chocobo carriage carrying the alchemical reagent hit a rock in the Sunway, causing the substance to explode. While no one was seriously injured in the accident, the entire shipment was lost, and now the Jolly Raptor must seek adventurers willing to travel to Nophica's Wells and slay djiggas until enough voidsent blood is collected again.

Popoto fields in the remote area of Nophica's Wells have fallen victim to feral flocks of ravenous dodos who rip up the plants' leaves, then dig up the tasty tubers with their powerful legs and beaks. In order to protect the fields which feed the sultanate, the Brass Blades are seeking adventurers willing to travel to the area, locate the flock, and slay the troublesome cloudkin before they can cause any further damage.

A pair of shape-shifting devilets imprisoned deep within the sultanate's dungeons for crimes most heinous have by some means escaped their chains and the magical wards surrounding their cells, and escaped the city via the subterranean sewer channels. If knowledge of a path leading from the dungeons to beyond the city walls were to fall into the wrong hands, the security of the city-state would become compromised, putting thousands of citizens in danger. The Brass Blades will handsomely reward any adventurer who can recapture or, if necessary, slay the voidsent, known to disguise themselves as galagos and control fire elemental familiars.

Ever since its theft from the forbidden tome vault deep beneath Frondale's Phrontistery, pages of the Necrologos─a dark scripture, the writings of which are said to serve as powerful wards preventing the escape of fell beasts trapped within─have been appearing in locations around Thanalan. It now is feared that those who stole the original tome have begun making copies, and if action is not taken quickly, the countryside could become overrun with deadly beasts summoned forth from the depths of the seven hells. While the Brass Blades continue to scour the realm in search of those who stole the original, the Phrontistery is calling for adventurers to aid in the destruction of loose pages littering the desert. All interested are to travel to Nophica's Wells and begin their search in the immediate area, taking care to slay any beasts that happen to be released from their fetters.

While collecting water from one of Nophica's Wells' many cenotes, a young Dunesfolk shepherd found a tattered scrap of parchment filled with arcane symbols and queer illustrations unlike anything the boy had ever seen. After being handed over to the local Brass Blades, the parchment was delivered to Frondale's Phrontistery, where it was determined to be a page from a stolen copy of the Necrologos─a forbidden tome said to contain wards which trap foul creatures within its bindings. Authorities at the Alchemists' Guild believe that there still may be pages scattered about the region and have petitioned adventurers to assist in conducting a thorough search, destroying all pages upon discovery, as well as any beasts which may be accidentally summoned forth from them.

A simple foray to Nophica's Wells to collect reagents turned bloody when a pair of young Alchemists' Guild initiates were attacked without provocation by a frenzied lightning elemental. The creature was slain shortly after the arrival of Brass Blades from nearby Camp Horizon, but not before one of the two acolytes had died of his injuries. Upon further inspection of the area, a page from a forbidden tome known as the Necrologos was found near where the elemental first appeared. To ensure that no more slips of the deadly parchment lie about the area, Frondale's Phrontistery is calling upon local adventurers to assist them in a massive sweep of Nophica's Wells. Those who find any of the pages are to destroy them immediately, as well as any more rogue creatures summoned therefrom.

A family of violent-natured peistes have made a den in the sacred mesa caverns of Halatali, preventing devoted Dunesfolk from making their pilgrimages to the holy site. In an attempt to rid the area of the pests, the Brass Blades are offering a generous reward to any adventurers willing to travel to the area in eastern Thanalan and slay the scalekin.

The Jolly Raptor is planning a shipment of fresh mongrel meat to the coeurl tamers on the Pearl, yet has been unable to procure enough of the pungent fodder after half of the sellswords hired to do the job ran off with the coin paid them in advance. The traders are now seeking adventurers to travel to Halatali and help them complete the order. Payment for services rendered will be received upon delivery of goods.

A mummers' extravaganza is being planned for the night before the Coliseum's next gladiatorial tournament, and the Rudius has been asked to provide the performers with several score brass knives to be used in their various attractions. Rudius proprietor Zagylswerd the Tall has neither the time nor coin to order the weapons from the smiths in Limsa Lominsa, and is rather hiring adventurers to seek out the blades of the ruffians roaming the mesas of Halatali...using whatever methods they feel appropriate.

Several of our esteemed employees working the mines of eastern Thanalan recently reported a brood of deadly peistes stalking them on their way to and from the pits, and in response, we sent a party of company swords to deal with the problem. While the swords were able to locate the beasts and engage them in battle, several escaped in the direction of Halatali, and have eluded capture. To assist those we have in pursuit, Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern is offering a generous reward to any brave adventurer who brings back the heads of these deadly scalekin.

A pair of devilets have broken into the sultanate's Royal Hall of Records and made away with several scrolls containing highly sensitive information. If these scrolls were to fall into the hands of the Amalj'aa, or worse, the Garlean Empire, it would compromise state security. To ensure this does not by any means happen, the Brass Blades are enlisting the aid of local adventurers to conduct a search of the realm to locate and eliminate the voidsent, known to disguise themselves as hedgemoles and control wind elemental familiars.

While on a pilgrimage to the sacred cave dwellings of Halatali, a Dunesfolk maiden discovered a tattered scrap of parchment filled with arcane symbols and queer illustrations unlike anything she had ever seen. After being entrusted to the local Brass Blades, the parchment was delivered to Frondale's Phrontistery, where it was determined to be a page from a stolen copy of the Necrologos─a forbidden tome said to contain wards which tether foul creatures within its bindings. Authorities at the Alchemists' Guild believe that there still may be pages scattered about the region and have petitioned adventurers to assist in conducting a thorough search, destroying all pages upon discovery, as well as any beasts that may be accidentally summoned forth from them.

As the Brass Blades are often required to rely on the assistance of adventurers, hedge knights, mercenaries, and sellswords to defend the sultanate, the royal guard will periodically conduct training exercises to ensure those hired men and women are ready when their services are called upon. One such exercise involving the culling of poisonous orobons is currently being planned in Halatali, and those interested are to report to the area's camp immediately. A small reward will be presented to all who complete the program.

Upon their passing, many of the city's dead are bound to the corporeal realm, their souls unable to make the journey to the realm of Thal and damned to walk the desert for all of eternity. Each day, these “zombies” rise from the desert to lament their imprisonment and torment the living─the task of silencing them falling to the Brass Blades and the sellswords they hire. Those interested in aiding the Blades are to report fully equipped to Halatali for further instructions.

An infestation of bloodplague-carrying djiggas has forced scores of devoted Dunesfolk to cut short their pilgrimages to the sacred caves of Halatali. If left unchecked, the infestation could grow even larger, and spread to nearby settlements such as Little Ala Mhigo and the Golden Bazaar. To prevent this, the Brass Blades are hiring sellswords to assist them in a sweep of the area to locate and terminate any vilekin.

A giant herd of aldgoats has come down from its home high atop nearby mountains and begun drinking up the scant trickle of water that passes through the area of Broken Water. To preserve the area's only supply of the life-sustaining liquid, the Brass Blades are petitioning adventurers to travel to the parched area in southern Thanalan and assist in the thinning of the aldgoat population.

Hedgemoles have begun burrowing tunnels underneath the few scattered creek beds near Camp Broken Water. Already several of these passageways have caved in, causing the precious water flowing in the creeks above to disappear below the surface, and leaving those few yeomen and shepherds who live in the area without a lifeline. The Brass Blades are calling for assistance in culling the prickly beasts before the area is left drier than it already is.

A crate of cockatrice eggs bound for Limsa Lominsa was dropped by a knock-kneed porter as it was being loaded onto a chocobo carriage, breaking nearly all of its fragile contents. The caravan cannot delay its departure much longer, and so the Jolly Raptor will be paying a premium for every cockatrice egg procured from Broken Water cockatrices and delivered to the traders posthaste.

After learning of a swarm of pestilent gnats infesting the caves of Little Ala Mhigo─a humble settlement that many of our valued employees call their home─a party of company swords was immediately sent to deal with the problem, only to lose sight of the vilekin as they passed through the southern canyons into the area of Broken Water. Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern, however, will not rest easy until the foul creatures have been found and exterminated, and therefore is offering a generous reward to anyone who will locate the gnats and finish the job.

Recently one of our fine men laboring in the Copperbell Mines accidentally discovered a pipe containing several ponzes of what may have been raw diamonds. Unfortunately, as the sack containing the stones was being carried back to Ul'dah for polishing, it was stolen by a shape-shifting devilet. The company swords entrusted to deliver the sack chased the voidsent all the way to Camp Broken Water where it flew into a pack of coblyns and proceeded to transform itself into one of the creatures. The men have been slaying all the coblyns they can find, but have yet to discover the imposter, and so Amajina & Sons is offering a reward for anyone who can.
