It now is feared that those who stole the original tome have begun making copies, and if action is not taken quickly, the countryside could become overrun with deadly beasts summoned forth from the depths of the seven hells. While the Brass Blades continue to scour the realm in search of those who stole the original, the sultanate is calling for adventurers to aid in the destruction of loose pages littering the desert. All interested are to travel to Camp Broken Water and begin their search in the immediate area, taking care to slay any beasts that happen to be released from their fetters.

As the Brass Blades are often required to rely on the assistance of adventurers, hedge knights, mercenaries, and sellswords to defend the sultanate, the royal guard will periodically conduct training exercises to ensure those hired men and women are ready when their services are called upon. One such exercise involving the culling of rabid mongrel hounds is currently being planned in Broken Water, and those interested are to report to the area's camp immediately. A small reward will be presented to all who complete the program.

As the Brass Blades are often required to rely on the assistance of adventurers, hedge knights, mercenaries, and sellswords to defend the sultanate, the royal guard will periodically conduct training exercises to ensure those hired men and women are ready when their services are called upon. One such exercise involving the culling of violent hedgemoles is currently being planned in Broken Water, and those interested are to report to the area's camp immediately. A small reward will be presented to all who complete the program.

In recent years, a lack of natural predators in the region has seen the number of peistes increase dramatically. To make matters worse, the scalekin are known to have a taste for plump, stout Lalafell, which they oft consume by swallowing whole, leaving the victims to digest slowly in their cavernous bellies. It is even said that the peiste's piercing howl is actually the screams of those recently devoured...  To ensure their numbers do not grow any further, the Brass Blades are seeking able-bodied adventurers to assist in the thinning of the peiste population. All those interested should, after reporting to Camp Broken Water, first collect several pieces of mongrel meat─another peiste favorite─then use the pungent flesh to lure the beasts from their lairs, and promptly proceed to slay them.

A puk infestation in the Nanawa Mines has Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern employees spending more time chasing off the bothersome scalekin than concentrating on what we pay them to do─mine ore. Company swords are doing what they can to cull the puks, but the sheer number of the flying pests is hampering our good men's efforts, and so we are temporarily hiring adventurers to travel to the Mines and aid in the extermination.

The Jolly Raptor is planning a shipment of gnat antennae to the witch doctors of Meracydia. Yet despite offering a reasonable reward, the traders have been unable to find sellswords willing or able to travel to the Nanawa Mines and slay the vilekin. To those seeking immediate employment, this an opportune chance to line your pockets with coin.

Brightash, mixed with clay to give it a soft glow, is highly sought after by potters across the realm, and often demands exorbitant prices. In an effort to advertise to all of Eorzea that they offer only quality goods at the lowest prices, the Jolly Raptor is planning to offer brightash at half the price of any other merchant. As they expect demand for the item to grow considerably for the duration of this offer, the traders are seeking adventurers to travel to the Nanawa Mines and help them stock their shelves.

Sightings of “restless spirits” have miners working Nanawa's pits too frightened to swing their pickaxes, resulting in a severe loss of profits for Amajina & Sons. Company swords have determined these spirits to be naught but stray will-o'-the-wisps wandered into the shafts from the nearby hills, but the miners refuse to work until all of them are gone. We cannot afford to stop the flow of ore into the sultanate, and so will handsomely reward any adventurers who travel to the mines to assist our men in exterminating the fiery voidsent.

Tunnels dug by antling workers have reached the lower levels of the Nanawa Mines, putting our employees stationed there in grave danger. Already, several miners have gone missing, and many more are afraid to come to work, fearing they, too, may be carried off to the antling's formicary. A party of company swords was dispatched to deal with the vilekin invaders, but the sheer number of tunnels and shafts has prevented the men from locating the elusive creatures, and therefore we are putting a call out to all able-bodied adventurers willing to lend their blades to help in exterminating the antlings.

A pair of deadly shape-shifting devilets charged with the deaths of several hundred of Thanalan's smallfolk have escaped from their unescapable cell in the Marasaja Pit. After conducting a realm-wide search to capture the villainous voidsent, the Brass Blades believe they finally have cornered them somewhere in the Nanawa Mines. To ensure that they do not let the criminals slip through their fingers, the Blades are seeking adventurers to assist in the search process, which involves collecting brightash from wisps and casting it on ladybugs─any of which could be the imps─to remove the creatures' glamours.

Ever since its theft from the forbidden tome vault deep beneath Frondale's Phrontistery, pages of the Necrologos─a dark scripture, the writings of which are said to serve as powerful wards preventing the escape of fell beasts trapped within─have been appearing in locations around Thanalan. It now is feared that those who stole the original tome have begun making copies, and if action is not taken quickly, the countryside could become overrun with deadly beasts summoned forth from the depths of the seven hells. While the Brass Blades continue to scour the realm in search of those who stole the original, the sultanate is calling for adventurers to aid in the destruction of loose pages littering the desert. All interested are to travel to the Nanawa Mines and begin their search in the immediate area, taking care to slay any beasts that happen to be released from their fetters.

Last night, an Amajina & Sons watchman making her rounds of the empty mines came across a soiled piece of parchment containing text written in a language unknown to the employee. As is required for anything found in the mines, she delivered the item to her supervisor, who, in turn, took it to the company assayers for inspection. When they could not decipher the queer markings, the assayers delivered the parchment to the Mineral Concern owners themselves, who, after much bickering, finally decided no amount of profit was worth risking their safety, and thus delivered it to Frondale's Phrontistery. There, the parchment was determined to be a page from the deadly Necrologos, and the guild immediately began hiring adventurers to travel to the Nanawa Mines, locate any more pieces of the tome, and destroy them and all beasts that are summoned therefrom.

Ever since a funguar wandered near her establishment and sprayed its spores all about, the proprietress of the Carline Canopy has been busy picking baby mushrooms from just about everything in the café. To prevent further fungal invasions, she is asking willing adventurers to travel to the nearby Camp Bentbranch and hunt down any stray funguars they can find.

Before commencing reforestation efforts in an area of Bentbranch that was burned in a recent thunderstorm, the Gods' Quiver is first petitioning adventurers to travel to the area and rid it of any pests which may pose a danger to the botanists to be sent in to plant saplings.

The area around Camp Bentbranch is overrun with deadly, blood-sucking chiglets, and the Holtwatch cannot deal with the problem on their own. Good coin is there for all adventurers willing to lend their sword in the cullings.

The Stillglade Fane is busy making preparations for this moon's Woodgreet Mass, and requires several evenfall fireflies to use in the Rites of Purification, in which two and ten of the luminous creatures are released from a basket over the Fane; their light believed to cleanse the sacred land and prepare it for ceremonies to follow.

The Stillglade Fane is busy making preparations for this moon's Woodgreet Mass, and requires the spores of several funguar to use in the Leafreading Ceremony, in which several of the brothers and sisters ingest the spores, which are said to give them the temporary power to “see” the messages left by the spirits in the leaves.

Increased sightings of spriggans near an area of forest in Bentbranch anointed by the Wood Wailers for clearing have Gridanian treecutters on edge, believing the beasts a warning from the forest. The brothers and the sisters have ensured the cutters that they have spoken with the Twelveswood and have its blessing, but the stubborn men and women refuse to work as long as the soulkin remain. The Wood Wailers will generously reward any who can assist in removing the spriggans from the area.

While meditating under the emerald canopy of the Black Shroud near Bentbranch, a party of pilgrims was assaulted by a labor of rabid moles. While two of the mendicants survived, one passed away before he could be saved by the local healers. To ensure the same fate does not befall others, the Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to travel into the wood, locate the pack, and exterminate it.

An unusually damp season has proven the perfect environment for deadly funguars to thrive. It is believed that if their numbers are allowed to continue growing, their spores will take root in many of the forest's giant sentinels, rotting the trees from the inside out. To protect them, the Holtwatch is calling on adventurers to journey to Bentbranch and cull the troublesome seedkin.

While meditating under the emerald canopy of the Black Shroud near Bentbranch, a party of devout pilgrims was assaulted by a swarm of deadly bees. While two of the mendicants survived, one passed away before he could be saved by the local healers. To ensure the same fate does not befall others, the Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to travel into the wood, locate the swarm, and exterminate it.

Before commencing reforestation efforts in an area of Emerald Moss where squatters cleared a large area of trees to build their shanty cabins, the Gods' Quiver is first petitioning adventurers to travel to the area and rid it of any pests which may pose a danger to the botanists who will be doing the replanting.

For the past few moons, there has been no end to terrifying reports of sand yarzon attacks on devout pilgrims come to worship in the Twelveswood. The Holtwatch is hiring all those with skill in hunting to flush the foreign vilekin out of their hiding places and fell the foul beasts.

While en route to Gridania, near Camp Emerald Moss, a caravan carrying a shipment of rare cogwheel ore was attacked by a band of thievish soulkin known as spriggans. While none of the caravan's escorts were harmed, most of the ore was carried off by the furry bandits. Black Rabbit Traders will pay a generous reward for any ore retrieved.

Perhaps in retaliation for the indiscriminate gathering of what they perceive as their “brothers,” a band of poisonous funguars recently sought their vengeance against several men and women out picking wild mushrooms near Camp Emerald Moss. To prevent any further attacks, travel to the camp and cull the spore-spouting seedkin.

After finding one of their Lalafell scouts near Camp Emerald Moss sucked dry of all his humours, the Holtwatch has vowed to do all they can to locate the culprits and make sure they can not repeat the vile deed. After further investigation of the corpse, several bite marks were found akin to those received when bitten by a chiglet. Travel to the camp, search the outlying area for any signs of a chiglet swarm, and upon discovery, eliminate the vilekin.

A trickster imp has taken to playing its deadly pranks on those Gridanians living on the outskirts of the city near Emerald Moss. There have already been several casualties, and the Holtwatch is hiring any who will lend their talents in subduing the voidsent villain. Those who accept this task are urged to take caution when engaging the imp, for it is known to often control familiars such as fireflies.

The incessant burrowing of moles has spread to several sapling farms, killing many of the young trees before they can be planted back in the Twelveswood. To ensure the safety of the remaining saplings, adventurers are being petitioned to travel to Camp Emerald Moss and quell the beastkin threat.

With increasing frequency, children who venture out into the wood near Emerald Moss to gather roots and berries are returning with large sores on their arms and legs, claiming they were stung by frenzied bees. To ensure the safety of their children, a group of parents is petitioning adventurers to seek out the vilekin and see that they do no more harm.

After a terrible blight which wiped out nearly a third of the trees in an area near Camp Tranquil, efforts to reforest the area have finally begun. Several packs of feral rodents, however, are putting a hamper on those efforts, attacking the botanists sent to the area to plant saplings. The Holtwatch is offering rewards to any adventurers willing to travel to the area and assist in the eradication of the pests.

Herds of antelopes have been spotted in several faerie apple orchards located on the fringes of Camp Tranquil, ignoring the fallen apples set aside for the beasts, and instead eating the unripe ones still on the trees. If this continues, there will not be enough apples left for the farmers to take to market, forcing them to struggle through the long winter. The Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to travel to the wooded area, locate the herd, and send as many of the beasts back to the forest as possible.

Since a renowned Ul'dahn alchemist's recent discovery of a tiny venom sac located in the tail of pterocs, demand for the item in alchemic circles has grown exponentially. To meet this demand, Black Rabbit Traders is petitioning adventurers to assist them in procuring freshly cut tails from the pterocs known to inhabit the dead trees and grots near Camp Tranquil.

n: A Feast Fit for a Queen
d: The Stillglade Fane is busy making preparations for this moon's Woodgreet Mass, and requires several queen bees to use during the Fasting Ceremony, in which brothers and sisters of the wood forsake all sustenance but that which was born of the forest. A generous reward awaits those who travel to Camp Tranquil and seek out honeybee hives from where the queens can be collected. The hives can often be found by locating the swarms of vilekin that hover near their homes.

Following an extended period of drought that saw many of the shallower creeks in Tranquil Paths dry up completely, a large number of river crabs has begun an exodus from the dried beds in search of fresh water. Unfortunately, the wavekin are known to be extremely violent, and there have already been reports of livestock going missing and children being attacked by the migrating wavekin. To ensure the safety of those who reside in the area, the Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to seek out the giant crustaceans and slay the creatures.

A party of murderous imps captured by a brave band of adventurers and handed over to the Gods' Quiver for imprisonment has escaped their chains and somehow stolen from the city. There have been sightings of the voidsent near Camp Tranquil, and the Holtwatch has already dispatched several units to subdue the imps. Their ability to disguise themselves in magicks, making them appear as harmless galagos has, however, hampered the Holtwatch's efforts, and forced the defenders of the Twelveswood to enlist the assistance of adventurers to help locate and recapture the escapees.

Only a fortnight after their capture and confinement in a heavily warded cell deep within Gridania's Spirithold Warden, a pair of deadly imps charged with the burning down of a sacred oak tree have escaped. It is believed that if not found soon, the voidsent will defile more of the forest, so the Gods' Quiver is petitioning adventurers to join in the search. The pair was last thought to have been seen in the vicinity of Tranquil Paths, but as the creatures possess magicks to make themselves appear as antelopes, the Holtwatch is not entirely certain of their whereabouts.

A pack of pterocs has been terrorizing the orchard tenders in Tranquil Paths. Normally pterocs will not attack a man unless they are near starving, but the size of these animals suggests that they have been eating well for quite some time. This has led the local Holtwatch to believe that the pack may be influenced by shape-shifting imps who have infiltrated the pack and become their leaders. If the imps are defeated, the pterocs' behavior will most likely return to normal; locating the voidsent in the pack, however, will be dangerous and time-consuming. Any adventurer interested in assisting in the capture of the shape-shifters is to report to Camp Tranquil. From there, he must first collect evenfall fireflies, whose glow can be used to dissolve the glamour of an imp. Once the pteroc pack is located and the imps are revealed, the creatures must be subdued before they have the chance to transform back into a beast.

A fire set by poachers to flush animals out of their dens and make them easier to catch has destroyed a large span of forest near Humblehearth. Efforts to reforest the area by local botanists, however, have been hampered by the unprovoked attacks of frenzied woodland creatures. To provide safety to the men and women working diligently to restore the wood to its former glory, the Gods' Quiver is calling for adventurers to aid in culling the ravenous beastkin.

n: From the Sea to the Trees
d: Recently, there have been reports of children being chased and even attacked by strange fish-like creatures flopping about the forest. Upon further inspection by local fishers, the culprits were determined to be none other than anglers and orobons, native to faraway Vylbrand. It is believed that the fish might be ones that were brought from the western island to keep as pets, but were released into the wild after growing too large for their aquarium. If allowed to breed, the invasive species could wreak havoc on the delicate ecosystem, endangering many of the weaker, native wavekin inhabiting the area. To quell the threat, the Gods' Quiver is petitioning adventurers to travel to Humblehearth, where the fish were last spotted, and assist in culling the creatures.

During the fall of Ala Mhigo, hundreds of refugees were forced to flee their homes, taking only what they could carry and leaving the rest of their possessions behind. Many of those who survived the exodus and found refuge in the hamlets of Coerthas and Thanalan, however, were soon faced with poverty, often lacking the coin to buy clothes enough to protect them from the elements. Black Rabbit Traders has heard their cries for help, and has devised a plan to help the Ala Mhigans while ridding the Twelveswood of troublesome poachers in the process. The outfit is hiring adventurers to seek out Humblehearth poachers and slay the criminals, then bring their jerkins back to the Black Rabbit so they can fix them up and sell them to the refugees at a price they can afford.

A pack of normally placid antelopes has grown frenzied, and has been reported assaulting botanists come to the wood to gather herbs. After inspecting the carcass of one of the beastkin, it is believed the animals must have eaten the leaves of the blackroot rose, known to cause horrible visions and induce extreme fits of violence. In their current state, the animals are a threat to themselves and the people of the forest, and so to prevent any further accidents, the Holtwatch has determined the antelopes must be put down, and are searching for adventurers willing to travel to Humblehearth and carry out the grim task.

Only two days after its capture and confinement in a heavily warded cell deep within Gridania's Spirithold Warden, a deadly imp charged with drowning a sacred antelope kept by the Stillglade Fane has escaped. It is believed that if not found soon, the voidsent will harm more of the forest's creatures, so the Gods' Quiver is petitioning adventurers to join in the search. The imp was last thought to have been seen in the vicinity of Humblehearth, but as the creature possesses magicks to make itself appear as a crab, the Holtwatch is not entirely certain of its whereabouts.

Pages from a copy of the Necrologos stolen from the Stillglade Fane's Green Athenaeum have turned up in Humblehearth. The tome is a dangerous work, filled with arcane wards that trap terrible beasts within the parchment, and if it were to fall into the wrong hands, it could be used to achieve unspeakable evils. This is why the Conjurers' Guild will stop at nothing to retrieve those pages and is offering a sizeable reward to any who can locate and destroy the forbidden writings, as well as any beasts summoned therefrom.

While picking mushrooms in Humblehearth, a Duskwight child found a tattered scrap of parchment filled with arcane symbols and queer illustrations unlike anything the boy had ever seen. After being handed over to the local Holtwatch, the parchment was delivered to the Stillglade Fane, where it was determined to be a page from a stolen copy of the Necrologos─a forbidden tome said to contain wards which trap foul creatures within its bindings. Authorities at the Conjurers' Guild believe that there still may be pages scattered about the region and have petitioned adventurers to assist in conducting a thorough search, destroying all pages upon discovery, as well as any beasts which may be accidentally summoned forth from them.

A brother of the Stillglade Fane assigned to the study of the Necrologos─a forbidden tome known to contain wards which bind arcane demons within its pages─was slowly infected by its evil taint, until one day his mind snapped and he dashed off into the forest, screaming in an unknown tongue and tearing pages from the book as he ran. The brother was found several days later, his body a dry husk, its humours drained from a thousand tiny holes. The pages, however, have yet to be gathered, and the Fane is worried that a similar fate awaits any who happen to stumble across them. To ensure this does not happen, the Conjurers' Guild is seeking brave adventurers to travel to Humblehearth, destroy as many pages as they can find, taking care not to accidentally summon forth any creatures.

A recent skirmish between a Gods' Quiver scouting party and a band of Ixali warriors left a vast swathe of the Twelveswood blackened, all life within the area reduced to cinders. A group of botanists has already been sent to the location to begin reforesting, but those efforts have been hampered by attacks from feral hogs displaced after the conflagration destroyed their homes. To see that the botanists can continue their work in peace, the Gods' Quiver is seeking adventurers to travel to Nine Ivies and slay the beastkin before they injure anyone.

Several terrible one-eyed creatures not of the Twelveswood have been spotted feeding on woodland creatures in the vicinity of Camp Nine Ivies. While not confirmed, the smallfolk believe the monsters to be none other than voidsent known as fachans. If there is truth to their tales, then it will not be long before the creatures turn their eyes to larger prey. The Gods' Quiver has already dispatched several advance parties into the forest, but are not ready to take any chances, and therefore are enlisting adventurers to aid them in the location and extermination of these foul invaders.

Orobon whiskers used by local healers in the concoction of powerful potations and unguents have had to be imported from the distant island of Vylbrand. Recently, though, rumors of the strange wavekin sloshing about the forest have begun surfacing in inns and pubs throughout Gridania. If the rumors are true, then this could be a prime opportunity to collect orobon whiskers locally. Black Rabbit Traders is hiring adventurers to travel to one of the locations mentioned in the rumors─Nine Ivies─and collect as many of the alchemical ingredients as possible.

The Twelveswood is home to countless varieties of efts; one giant variety, however, thought to have been recently introduced by traders from Garlemald, is slowly driving the native species to extinction by consuming all the food normally distributed evenly amongst them. To preserve the diversity of the forest, the Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to travel to Camp Nine Ivies and assist in thinning the eft population.

A shape-shifting devilet being held within Gridania for crimes of thievery and defilement of the forest has somehow broken free of its bonds and fled the city-state. A wood-wide search for it is already underway, but so far there have been no sightings of the voidsent, known to wear a magick glamour allowing it to take the appearance of an innocent dormouse. To assist in the search, the various branches of the Holtwatch are calling upon adventurers and will handsomely reward the ones who bring the devilet back to justice...be it alive or dead.

A copy of the forbidden Necrologos─a powerful tome known to contain violent beasts trapped within its pages by arcane wards woven in the writings─has been stolen from Stillglade Fane's Green Athenaeum. Fortunately, it appears the thieves did not know what they had in their hands, and discarded the book as they passed through Nine Ivies. Unfortunately, the book was then found by some woodland beast which proceeded to tear the binding apart in its jaws, scattering the pages about the area. There is still the chance that these pages may be found by those with ill intentions, and so the Conjurers' Guild is petitioning adventurers to travel to Nine Ivies and locate the missing pages, destroying them and any monsters summoned therefrom upon discovery.

An increased number of fires in Nine Ivies has the Holtwatch worried that their daily patrols through the area are not sufficient in finding all of the threats to the forest. To increase security, the Gods' Quiver is seeking experienced Disciples of War and Magic to travel to the area's staging points and deal with any threats that may appear.

n: All Nine Ivies is a Stage
d: The Gods' Quiver has broken ground on the construction of a staging area to be used as a checkpoint for patrol units passing through Nine Ivies. Progress on the site, however, has been slow due to repeated attacks from malicious airborne pests determined to prevent the guild from completing its task. To allow the men and women to concentrate on their work, the Gods' Quiver is seeking adventurers skilled in the disciplines of war and magic to defend the perimeter in short shifts until the staging area is built.

As the Holtwatch is often required to rely on the assistance of adventurers, hedge knights, mercenaries, and sellswords to defend the Twelveswood, the Wood Wailers and Gods' Quiver will periodically conduct training exercises to ensure those hired men and women are ready when their services are called upon. One such exercise to cull ravenous slugs is currently being planned in Nine Ivies, and those interested are to report to the area's camp immediately. A small reward will be presented to all who complete the program.

A warm winter and a damp spring have resulted in an explosion in the number of dreamtoads living in the ponds and lakes near Treespeak. The ravenous scalekin, which have few natural predators, have already begun devouring the area's flora, and there are even reports that the toads have been eating some of the area's smaller fauna as well. To maintain the balance of the fragile ecosystem, the Gods' Quiver is seeking adventurers willing to assist in culling the cyclopean creatures.

A shipment of rare canopy apples bound for Ul'dah has been plundered by a pack of feral lemurs. Rather than undertaking the nigh on impossible task of locating another farmer growing the fruit, Black Rabbit Traders believes it may be easier to locate the animals who snatched the cargo, as it is well documented that lemurs often hoard their food rather than eat it right away. Thus, the organization will generously reward any who travel to Treespeak and help retrieve the lost produce.

Black Rabbit Traders is preparing a shipment of blacksand, valued by the alchemists of Ul'dah for use in their sand baths, as it is believed it distributes heat more evenly than the regular desert variety. Blacksand, however, only occurs deep below the forest bed, therefore making it difficult to find without a lot of digging and even more luck. There is a more effective way to obtain the item, though, and that is from the claws of hedgemoles who burrow incessantly beneath the forest, destroying roots of the sacred sentinels which make up the Shroud's canopy. Black Rabbit Traders is seeking able-bodied volunteers to travel to Treespeak and assist in not only collecting blacksand for their shipment, but also helping preserve the forest's gentle giants by seeking out and slaying hedgemoles.

Late last night, a knab of ravenous dreamtoads attacked the livestock pens of a small commune situated on the shores of Fallgourd Lake near Treespeak. The pilgrims residing at the commune confronted the monstrous entities, but the creatures escaped, and now the men and women fear that the scalekin may return again soon and attack the rest of their few remaining animals...or even worse, the children or the elderly. To prevent this, they have petitioned the Holtwatch to come find and slay the creatures, and the Holtwatch in turn is seeking adventurers who will travel to Treespeak in their stead, offering a generous reward for any dreamtoads dispatched.

Murderous devilets known to possess powerful magicks that allow them to take on the shape of other creatures have escaped from a heavily warded cell in Gridania's Spirithold, a prison used to hold enemies of the forest while they await their arboreal judgment. To assist in the recapturing of the changelings, the Spirithold warden, Polga Molga, is hiring sellswords to scour the area of Emerald Moss and locate the voidsent using lightning orbs to dissolve their glamours. All those with the courage to accept the challenge are to report to Camp Emerald Moss at once, and after collecting the orbs needed to uncover the devilets, are to seek out any suspicious-looking crabs and use the orbs on them. Once the voidsent have shown their true colors, they are to be taken with force.

Pages from a copy of the Necrologos stolen from the Stillglade Fane's Green Athenaeum have turned up in Treespeak. The tome is a dangerous work, filled with arcane wards that trap terrible beasts within the parchment, and if it were to fall into the wrong hands, could be used to achieve unspeakable evils. This is why the Conjurers' Guild will stop at nothing to retrieve those pages and is offering a sizeable reward to any who can locate and destroy the forbidden writings, as well as any beasts summoned therefrom.

The Gods' Quiver has broken ground on the construction of a staging area to be used as a checkpoint for patrol units passing through Treespeak. Progress on the site, however, has been slow due to repeated attacks from malicious flying monsters determined to prevent the guild from completing its task. To allow the men and women to concentrate on their work, the Gods' Quiver is seeking adventurers skilled in the disciplines of war and magic to defend the perimeter in short shifts until the staging area is built.

An archer from the Gods' Quiver assigned to help in the construction of a staging point near Treespeak was violently attacked by a pack of bloodthirsty scalekin while felling logs not half a malm from the site. Her fellow bows sought permission to seek out the culprits and fill them full of arrows, but their party commander denied the request, insisting that they first finish building the outpost. Since then, the men and women have not been able to sleep easy, knowing the monsters who harmed their sister still roam free, and have put together a reward that will be presented to any adventurer who can seek out and slay the scalekin.

Though poaching is one of the most severe crimes in the Twelveswood, often punishable by death, there is no end to the constant flow of those who come to the sacred forest in search of exotic pelts and horns to sell to dubious traders from the Far East. The sheer number of the criminals is forcing the Gods' Quiver to allocate far more men and women than they can spare, and so to lighten their load, they seek able-bodied adventurers to assist in patrolling at least six areas near Treespeak and dealing “swift justice” to any of these forsaken hunters that can be found.

A litter of puks was recently found nesting inside one of the tunning chambers in the MunTuy Cellars. Before a Gods' Quiver party could arrive to send the animals back to the soil, however, the scalekin had all voided the vat and are now believed to be hiding somewhere in the nooks and crannies of the subterranean tunnels. Already one of the cellarkeeps has gone missing, and another lost his ear when something attacked him while making his daily inspection of the wizening chambers. With the safety of the cellarkeeps at stake, the Gods' Quiver has put out a call to adventurers to assist in locating and exterminating the airborne pests.

An informant from Ul'dah has provided representatives from Black Rabbit Traders with a rumor that the Jolly Raptor is planning a shipment of gnat antennae to the witch doctors of Meracydia, and that the company has been promised an exorbitant sum of gil upon its delivery. The Black Rabbit does not believe that their rivals should have the privilege to horde all the profits, and so has begun planning a shipment of their own. To carry out their plan, they require the assistance of able-bodied adventurers to travel to the MunTuy Cellars and collect as many of the antennae as possible, as quickly as possible, for time is of the essence!

The Stillglade Fane is busy making preparations for this moon's Woodgreet Mass, and requires several earth orbs to use in the Loam Eye ceremony, in which those brothers and sisters newly come to the Fane are blessed with leaf and soil, opening their inner eye to the Land around them. The forest has granted its children leave to retrieve the orbs from the elemental spirits which inhabit the depths of the MunTuy Cellars, and the Fane is seeking brave adventurers to travel to the tunnels and collect the sacred items.

A pack of wolves has been spotted stalking through the streets of Gridania, leaving many residents of the city-state in fear of leaving their homes at night lest they fall victim to an attack by the beastkin. The Holtwatch has tracked the pack for a fortnight and believes its den is located somewhere deep within the MunTuy Cellars. The guards now are seeking adventurers to join them in a sweep of the tunnels to flush out and put down the pack before the animals can do any harm.

A recent flood left several of the deeper chambers in the MunTuy Cellars filled waist-deep with water, transforming them into a prime habitat for deadly delta crabs. The waters have since receded, yet the carnivorous wavekin still remain, and they have grown restless searching for prey in the relatively empty tunnels. This has many of the cellarkeeps on edge, with some even refusing to see to their daily tasks for fear of their lives, and as a result, scores of MunTuy vats lie unchecked, their contents on the verge of spoilage. To ensure the safety of the cellarkeeps and the livelihoods of the vat owners, the Holtwatch is petitioning adventurers to delve into the subterranean labyrinth, seek out the crabs, and slay the crustaceans.

Two shape-shifting devilets being held within Gridania for crimes of murder and defilement of the forest have somehow broken free of their bonds and fled the city-state. A wood-wide search for them is already underway, but so far there have been no sightings of the voidsent, known to wear magick glamours allowing them to take the appearance of innocent ladybugs. To assist in the search, the various branches of the Holtwatch are calling upon adventurers and will handsomely reward the ones who bring the devilets back to justice...be it alive or dead.

Two nights past, the bodies of a cellarkeep and what appeared to be his mistress were found mutilated beyond recognition in one of the lower ripening chambers of the MunTuy Cellars. Along with the bodies, a burned piece of parchment was found lying behind one of the chamber's many vats─a piece of parchment that, after further inspection by a brother of the Stillglade Fane, turned out to be none other than a page from a copy of the Necrologos recently stolen from the Fane's Green Athenaeum. The tome in question is said to contain foul demons trapped within the arcane wards inscribed on its pages, and could prove a deadly weapon if it were to fall into the wrong hands. This is why the Stillglade Fane is offering a sizeable reward to anyone who finds and destroys other loose pages in the Cellars, slaying all beasts which are summoned therefrom.

A copy of the forbidden Necrologos─a powerful tome known to contain violent beasts trapped within its pages by arcane wards woven in the writings─has been stolen from Stillglade Fane's Green Athenaeum. Fortunately, it appears the thieves either discarded or dropped the book while hiding in the MunTuy Cellars. Unfortunately, the book was then found by a cellar puk which proceeded to tear the binding apart in its jaws, scattering the pages about the area. There is a chance that the nibbling of the parchment may have weakened the wards, and so the Conjurers' Guild is petitioning adventurers to travel to the Cellars and locate the missing pages, destroying them and any monsters summoned therefrom upon discovery.

Thalassocratic Navy captain and reputed sword enthusiast Baron Gustav von Gustberg III recently paid a visit to Naldiq & Vymelli's seeking to purchase a new weapon. Several other orders from equally important clients, however, have the forge's smithies working night and day. Loath to arouse the displeasure of such an influential patron and risk losing his custom, the guild seeks a skilled blacksmith to complete his order in timely fashion.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: To protect her ship against ambushes by pirates and Sahagin alike, Captain Oya of the Twilight Rose has hired several mercenaries to accompany her crew on its next voyage. To ensure the mercenaries have enough equipment to fend off any threats, the captain is currently looking to restock her armory with spare weapon parts and is searching for skilled blacksmiths to create the items.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Aergwynt's ship was badly damaged in a recent storm and his fellow crew members lack the tools needed to make the necessary repairs. For reasons he would rather not mention, Aergwynt cannot simply purchase the relevant tools, but requires that they be crafted for him instead, using materials of his own provision.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Betrayal by a trusted supplier has resulted in a crate of ingots originally promised to Dympna Tinstyll being purchased by the Brugaire Consortium, leaving the independent exporter scrambling to gather more ore before her commissioned cargo ship leaves port for Gridania. Any assistance in smelting new ingots will be generously rewarded.
client: Independent Exporter of Exotics, Dympna Tinstyll
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Drowning Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers is looking to spruce up his alehouse, and has decided that it is missing a few good, brutish-looking swords hanging from its walls to intimidate any patrons looking to start trouble. As a gesture of kindness to his good friend Baderon, Camp Bearded Rock Gatewarden and loyal Wench patron Didiwai has agreed to provide the materials to make the sword. Now, Baderon only needs you to make it. Speak with Didiwai to receive the materials, and present the gatewarden with the mock weapon upon completion.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: To provide affordable accoutrements to fledgling adventurers, Drowning Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers purchases leftover supplies from the Yellowjackets stationed at Camp Bearded Rock, and hires the weavers who frequent his establishment to synthesize new clothes. Speak with Gatewarden Didiwai to receive the supplies, and present him with the goods upon completion.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: The counters at the Drowning Wench have seen better days, and alehouse proprietor Baderon Tenfingers would like to replace their tops before someone is gravely injured in a rogue splinter incident. As a gesture of kindness to his good friend Baderon, Camp Bearded Rock Gatewarden and loyal Wench patron Didiwai has agreed to provide the logs with which to make the lumber. Now, Baderon only needs you to do the carving. Speak with Didiwai to receive the materials, and present the gatewarden with the planks upon completion.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: To provide fledgling adventurers with affordable footwear for their journeys into the wild, Drowning Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers purchases leftover supplies from the Yellowjackets stationed at Camp Bearded Rock, and hires the talented leatherworkers who frequent his establishment to synthesize new shoes. Speak with Gatewarden Didiwai to receive the supplies, and present him with the goods upon completion.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Of the scores of new adventurers who come wandering into the Drowning Wench every day, only a handful ever survive the rigors of the wild, a large reason being their lack of proper equipment. To ensure that his customers survive the day so they can return to the pub to spend their coin at night, Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers has begun the lease of barbuts to those of his customers not yet endowed enough to purchase headgear of their own. Unfortunately, upon their return, many of the helms are in dire need of repair, leaving Baderon in constant need of rivets. All armorers interested in filling his or her purse with some extra gil should travel to Camp Bearded Rock and speak with Gatewarden Didiwai to receive the materials necessary, and upon creating the parts, return to Didiwai so he may inspect the final product.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Drowning Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers' trademark bone rings have caught the eye of many an adventurer, spurring the outspoken alemaster to begin selling replicas in his pub. He now requires the assistance of talented goldsmiths to assist him in maintaining his stock, and is willing to pay a handsome reward to those who do. If interested, travel to Camp Bearded Rock and speak with Gatewarden Didiwai to receive the materials necessary to perform the synthesis. Once the product is finished, hand them over to Didiwai for inspection.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: After hearing patron after patron complain of having to walk in footwear worn down from long journeys across the realm, Baderon Tenfingers of the Drowning Wench vowed he would find a way to assist the sore-footed men and women. His solution was providing customers with rubber soles that could be attached to the bottom of shoes and boots, not only providing cushion for the foot, but also extending the life of the footwear. This idea turned out to be an instant hit, and now Baderon will pay good coin to any skilled alchemists willing to help him maintain his stock. All interested in the proposition are to travel to Camp Bearded Rock and speak with Gatewarden Didiwai to receive the necessary materials for the synthesis. When the items are complete, return them to Didiwai for inspection.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: There is nothing like a good morning meal to strengthen the body and warm the soul. To ensure that his patrons have the energy to return to his establishment after a long day of adventuring, Drowning Wench proprietor Baderon Tenfingers requires several servings of piping hot frumenty and is willing to pay talented culinarians a share of his profits for assisting him in the making of the dish. Procure the materials needed to complete the synthesis from Camp Bearded Rock Gatewarden Didiwai, and present the completed product to him for inspection.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Betrayal by a trusted supplier has resulted in a crate of ingots originally promised to the Brugaire Consortium being purchased by independent exporter Dympna Tinstyll, leaving the outfit scrambling to gather more ore before its commissioned cargo ship leaves port for Gridania. Any assistance in smelting new ingots will be generously rewarded.
client: Brugaire Consortium Junior Archivist, Bango Zango

For reasons she would rather not mention, H'rhanbolo cannot simply purchase the relevant supplies, but requires that they be crafted for her instead, using materials of her own provision.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: To protect his ship against ambushes by pirates and Sahagin alike, the captain of the cargo ship Dawn Trader has hired several mercenaries to accompany his crew on its next voyage. To ensure the mercenaries have enough equipment to fend off any threats, ship storesman Leveridge Halborn is currently looking to restock his armory with spare weapons and is searching for skilled blacksmiths to create the items.
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: While fair weather is often considered a fisher's best friend, the relentless beating of the sun's rays can prove quite the annoyance when trying to work out on the open seas, far from shade. As a result, high-quality hats designed to block out the sun are constantly in demand. To answer the call of their fellow Lominsans, the Brugaire Consortium is hard at work day and night procuring new headwear. They cannot, however, meet their orders alone, and have put out a plea calling for the assistance of skilled weavers. Speak with junior archivist Bango Zango to receive the materials necessary to start hatting.
client: Brugaire Consortium Junior Archivist, Bango Zango
obj: Create and deliver the following items:

d: Warm currents from the south have brought with them massive schools of palm squid, and have local fishers scrambling to outfit their boats with equipment used in catching the scrumptious cephalopods. To profit from this sudden increase in demand, the Brugaire Consortium is calling upon skilled carpenters to assist in the crafting of new fishing supplies. Speak with junior archivist Bango Zango to receive the materials necessary to begin.
client: Brugaire Consortium Junior Archivist, Bango Zango
